sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I'm Emily, your host. Today,
we are traveling to Nairobi, the capital city of Kenya. Nairobi is a city full of life,
colors, and smiles. It's a place where nature and city life meet. Let's explore this exciting
area. Here is Nairobi. Nairobi is in the east of Africa. It is the capital and largest city
of Kenya. The city sits at a high altitude, about 1,800 meters above sea level. That means
the weather is cooler than in many other African cities. It is also close to national parks
full of wild animals. Part three, a short history. Nairobi was founded in 1899 as a small railway
station. It quickly grew into an important trade and travel center. During the British colonial
period, it became the capital of Kenya. After Kenya's independence in 1963,
Nairobi continued to grow. Today, it is one of the biggest and most modern cities in Africa.
Part four, what does Nairobi look like? Nairobi is a mix of nature and tall buildings.
In the city center, you see offices, hotels, and busy streets. But only a short drive away,
you find green parks and open grasslands. The most famous is Nairobi National Park right
next to the city. You can see lions, zebras, and giraffes with skyscrapers in the background.
Amazing. Part five, the people of Nairobi. The people of Nairobi are friendly and welcoming.
They come from many different ethnic groups and speak several languages.
The main language is Swahili, but most people also speak English. You'll often hear greetings
like Jumbo or Habari, both mean hello. People here are proud of their culture
and love to share it with visitors. Part six, life in Nairobi. Nairobi is a city that never sleeps.
There are markets, cafes, and music everywhere. People go to work in offices or shops,
and students walk to school in uniforms. On weekends, families visit parks, go shopping,
or take short trips to the countryside. It's a busy, happy city full of energy and sound.
Part seven, food in Nairobi. Kenyan food is delicious and simple.
A popular dish is Zugali, made from corn flour. It is eaten with vegetables, meat, or fish.
People also enjoy nyama choma, which means grilled meat. You'll see people cooking it outside on
charcoal grills. Fresh fruits like mangoes, pineapples, and bananas are everywhere.
Part eight, nature around Nairobi. Nature is very close to daily life in Nairobi.
You can visit the Nairobi National Park to see wild animals. Another popular place is the Giraffe
Center, where you can feed giraffes by hand. There's also the David Sheldrick elephant orphanage,
where baby elephants are cared for. It's a city where humans and animals live side by side.
Part nine, culture and music. Nairobi is also a center of Kenyan culture and art. Music is
everywhere. People love benga, Afrobeat, and Swahili pop. You can hear drums, dancing,
and joyful singing in many places. There are also art galleries and theaters that show Kenyan
creativity. Nairobi's youth love fashion and modern African design. Part 10, weather in Nairobi.
Nairobi has a mild climate all year round. It's not too hot and not too cold. There are
two rainy seasons, one in April and one in November. The rest of the year, the weather is sunny and
pleasant. When it rains, everything turns green and fresh again. Part 11, special places to visit.
If you visit Nairobi, don't miss Nairobi National Park to see wild animals near the city.
Karen Blixen Museum, the house of the author of Out of Africa,
Giraffe Center, to meet friendly giraffes, Kenyatta International Conference Center,
for a great view of the city, Maasai Market, for colorful handmade crafts and jewelry.
Every place shows a different side of Nairobi. Part 12, thank you for joining me in Nairobi, Kenya.
It is a city full of nature, culture, and energy. From the sound of music to the side of giraffes,
Nairobi is truly special. If you want to feel Africa's heart, come to Nairobi.
Goodbye, or as people in Swahili say, Kwahiri.
